skim: Spain logged its first data breach executed end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent, prompting regulators to call for an immediate review of security models.
A joint investigation tied a covert Israeli intelligence-linked influence campaign to years of anti-Qatar disinformation launched in the days after October 7, 2023.
The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75–4% under new Chair Kevin Warsh, the first hike since 2023, as the 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 5%.
The US House passed a bill empowering Trump to impose 100% tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy, squarely targeting India and China.
Bangladesh's measles epidemic passed 1,000 deaths despite an emergency campaign that delivered nearly 20 million vaccine doses.

stories.headline: Bangladesh’s Measles Epidemic Passes 1,000 Deaths as Vaccination Gaps Persist
stories.body: Bangladesh’s measles outbreak has killed at least 1,009 children since mid-March despite an emergency campaign that delivered nearly 20 million vaccine doses, per Al Jazeera (Sep 14). Health officials say 83% of the dead had never been vaccinated, with coverage eroded by 2024’s political upheaval; “you have to maintain equity,” said Mushtuq Hussain, a former principal scientific officer at the country’s disease-control institute, as authorities prepare another vaccination round to close remaining immunity gaps.

stories.headline: Gold Mine Collapse Kills at Least 67 in Sudan’s RSF-Held West Kordofan
stories.body: A gold mine collapsed late Tuesday at the al-Zara site near Nuhud in Sudan’s West Kordofan province, killing at least 67 people, with rescuers still searching for others trapped in the shafts, per TimesLIVE (Sep 16). The mine lies in territory held by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces; survivor Khairal-Sayed Gabara called the collapse “massive” and said the machinery needed to clear debris “wasn’t readily available,” underscoring the weak safety standards at Sudan’s informal gold mines, which have collapsed repeatedly in recent years.

stories.headline: Police Fire Tear Gas as DR Congo Protesters Reject Tshisekedi’s Bid for a Third Term
stories.body: Police used tear gas and arrested at least ten people as opposition-led protests swept Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and Uvira on Tuesday against a proposed constitutional amendment that would let President Félix Tshisekedi seek a third term, per Al Jazeera (Sep 15). The “C64” opposition coalition organized the nationwide action after parliament adopted a bill in June opening the door to changing term limits by referendum; coalition figure Mohamed Eyenga said “many of our activists were unfortunately and arbitrarily arrested,” while a provincial police commander insisted only violent demonstrators were detained.

stories.headline: Corruption Allegations Engulf Brazil’s Supreme Court Ahead of October Election
stories.body: Brazil’s Supreme Court faces an institutional crisis after the collapse of Banco Master, a bank with up to $16 billion in assets, exposed conflicts of interest among justices weeks before October’s presidential election, per KSAT (Sep 14). Justice Alexandre de Moraes’s wife held a $23 million legal contract with the failed bank while Justice André Mendonça is accused of selectively leaking case details to benefit Senator Flávio Bolsonaro; “because it’s an extremely polarized campaign, all that is negative for de Moraes is, immediately, positive for the Bolsonaro family,” said political consultant Thomas Traumann.

stories.headline: Asia Cup Trophy Row Escalates as Naqvi Rejects Apology
stories.body: ACC president Mohsin Naqvi flatly denied apologising to the BCCI, saying “I have done nothing wrong and I have never apologised to the BCCI nor will I ever do so,” and instead invited India to collect the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from the ACC’s Dubai office, per Eastern Herald (Sep 16). India’s players had snubbed the trophy on stage after beating Sri Lanka in the September 13 final, objecting to Naqvi’s dual role as Pakistan’s interior minister, and the BCCI says it will raise the standoff at the ICC’s October meeting.

stories.headline: Gill to Lead India’s ODIs, Two Uncapped Players Named for West Indies
stories.body: India have named uncapped Auqib Nabi and Naman Dhir in their ODI squad for the home series against West Indies, with Shubman Gill leading the 50-over side and Shreyas Iyer captaining the T20Is, per ICC.com (Sep 16). Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli remain in the ODI group as India “begin building momentum” toward the 2027 World Cup, while Mayank Yadav returns to the T20I bowling attack.

stories.headline: Sunderland Mark Europe Return With Le Fée Penalty Win
stories.body: Enzo Le Fée converted a 64th-minute penalty to give Sunderland a 1-0 win over AZ Alkmaar, sealing the Black Cats’ first European points on their return to continental football after a 53-year absence, per VAVEL (Sep 16). Le Fée made amends for a penalty miss the previous weekend, sending this one into the same corner, while substitute Brian Brobbey made his Europa League debut for the club late on.

stories.headline: Benfica Stun AC Milan for First-Ever Win Over the Rossoneri
stories.body: Dodi Lukebakio and Jakub Kaminski scored either side of half-time as Benfica beat AC Milan 2-0 at San Siro — the Portuguese side’s first win over Milan in seven meetings — per Flashscore (Sep 16). Milan boss Rubén Amorim threw on Christian Pulisic at half-time in search of a response, but Benfica’s defence held firm as Souffian El Karouani was named man of the match in the Europa League opener.

stories.headline: Ferrari Duo Test at Imola as F1 Weighs It for Season Finale
stories.body: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc ran a two-day Pirelli tyre test at Imola on September 15-16 alongside a junior-driver programme, even as F1 boss Stefano Domenicali confirmed the circuit is in the mix to host the European season finale if the Qatar and Abu Dhabi rounds fall through, per PlanetF1 (Sep 14). “Imola is in the basket, but it is not defined—it is in the options,” Domenicali said, with a decision expected once the calendar situation clarifies.

stories.headline: Fed Hikes Rates to 3.75%–4%, First Increase Since 2023
stories.body: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate 25 basis points to a 3.75%–4% range, and Chair Kevin Warsh said “the plain fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long.” The Dow sank roughly 600 points (1.2%), the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 5% for the first time since 2007, even as August retail sales beat expectations at 1.2% growth; per Yahoo Finance (Sep 16).

stories.headline: Amazon Locks In Up to $8B Generac Deal for Data-Center Backup Power
stories.body: Amazon signed a long-term supply agreement with Generac worth up to $8 billion for backup generators at its data centers, with $2.4 billion of deliveries slated for 2027–2028. As part of the pact Amazon received warrants for up to 1.69 million Generac shares at $200.93 apiece, and Generac stock surged as much as 40% in after-hours trading; per Briefs/Investing.com (Sep 16).

stories.headline: Oracle Cuts Staff Again in Third Layoff Round of 2026
stories.body: Oracle sent a fresh wave of 6am termination emails with same-day effective dates, its third workforce reduction of the year following cuts in April and August. One email read: “After careful consideration of Oracle’s current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change — today is your last working day.” Per Deccan Herald (Sep 15).

stories.headline: Spain Logs First Data Breach Executed End-to-End by an AI Agent
stories.body: Spain’s data protection authority (AEPD) confirmed the country’s first breach carried out entirely by an autonomous AI agent, which scanned for access, ran vulnerability checks and chained the steps together to reach files with personal data and invoices without human intervention. AEPD deputy Francisco Pérez Bes said “the arrival of AI agents in the offensive arena should prompt an immediate review of security and data protection models,” while stressing “human supervision remains essential.” Per The Register (Sep 16).

stories.headline: OpenAI in Talks for $1.2 Trillion Valuation, Altman Rules Out 2026 IPO
stories.body: OpenAI is in early talks with investors on a new funding round that would value the company near $1.2 trillion, up sharply from the $852 billion mark set in its March round that raised $122 billion. CEO Sam Altman said OpenAI will not go public in 2026, citing AI-safety concerns as the reason to stay private for now; per Benzinga, citing the Financial Times (Sep 16).

stories.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind Detail Safety Coordination Plans
stories.body: The three labs moved to formalize their weeks of safety talks: OpenAI said it will join Anthropic in embedding independent evaluators, and the firms are working toward an industry standards body to screen advanced models and coordinate slowdowns if risk escalates. OpenAI policy chief Chris Lehane said the companies “do not require a government waiver to continue their safety coordination,” while Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk all backed Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s proposal to collectively slow frontier development; per The AI Insider (Sep 16).

stories.headline: Huang Dismisses Anthropic’s Call for AI Antitrust Waivers
stories.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back on Dario Amodei’s push for antitrust waivers to let labs coordinate on safety, calling new rules “completely unnecessary” since “we have plenty of laws…that govern the reliability and functionality of products.” He added, “we’re not going to die in 2030,” extending his earlier dismissal of AI extinction warnings; per Benzinga (Sep 16).

stories.headline: Revolut Hackers Slash Ransom to $3M, Switch to Monero, Set 24-Hour Deadline
stories.body: The group behind the Revolut breach cut its demand from 10,000 bitcoin (~$780M) to roughly 6,000 Monero (~$3M) with a 24-hour deadline, shifting to the privacy coin because, as reporting noted, “Monero is designed to defeat that tracking.” The stolen data — passports, driving licenses, selfies, IBANs and full bitcoin histories for 680 customers across 32 countries — was obtained by impersonating Italy’s Ministry of Interior through its certified-email system, passing SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks; the UK’s ICO and FCA are now investigating. Per CryptoTimes (Sep 17).

stories.headline: Trump Calls Canada’s Possible EU ‘Associate Member’ Status a ‘Hostile Act’
stories.body: President Trump threatened new tariffs on the European Union after EU Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen floated creating an “associate member” status for Canada as Ottawa seeks closer ties with Europe amid its trade dispute with Washington. “If it’s a good intention, that’s fine. If it’s a bad intention, we’ll put very heavy tariffs,” Trump said, dismissing the idea as “laughable” and calling Canada a “terrible trade partner,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 17). A Canada-EU summit is planned for Montreal next month.

stories.headline: Egypt’s Sisi Rejects Palestinian Displacement as Abbas Visits Cairo
stories.body: Hosting Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas in Cairo, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi reaffirmed “Egypt’s firm stance against the displacement of the Palestinian people or any attempt to annihilate the Palestinian cause,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 16). The meeting came after Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said the military would “finish the job” in Gaza so it could “implement the migration plan,” and as Israel advances the E1 settlement project between Jerusalem and Maale Adumim.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia Vows ‘Firm’ Response After Houthi Strikes Wound 13
stories.body: Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif wounded 13 civilians and damaged homes and vehicles, prompting coalition spokesperson Major-General Turki al-Maliki to warn that “the Joint Forces Command of the Coalition will deal with these attacks responsibly and firmly to protect the sovereignty of the kingdom,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 15). The Houthis claimed Saudi Arabia carried out 54 air raids in 24 hours, as the UN reported 125,000 people newly displaced in Yemen since early September.

stories.headline: Zelensky Says He’s Ready to Meet Putin at December G20 in Miami
stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would meet Vladimir Putin at the G20 summit in Miami if the Russian leader attends, telling reporters “we have to come, we have to meet, to speak and make decisions,” per Kyiv Independent (Sep 12). The two have not met in person since before Russia’s 2022 invasion; Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Moscow hasn’t decided on attendance, while Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov countered that Zelensky should instead travel to Moscow.

stories.headline: China Steps Up Military Pressure on Taiwan Ahead of Xi’s Washington Trip
stories.body: Taiwan tracked PLA aircraft and naval vessels entering its air defense zones on multiple days this month — including seven aircraft and six ships on Sep 12 and four aircraft with six vessels on Sep 13-14 — per the Daily Caller (Sep 14). Patrick Cronin of the Hudson Institute said the operations show “China is demonstrating an ever-improving military capacity to take Taiwan by force,” as Xi Jinping prepares for a September 24 state visit to Washington with a large Chinese business delegation.

fixtures.headline: England Chase Series Win in Cardiff T20I
fixtures.body: England, 1-0 up after Harry Brook’s 119-run rout in the series opener, face Sri Lanka in the 2nd T20I at Sophia Gardens, Cardiff, on September 17, with two more T20Is and three ODIs to follow before the series wraps on September 27.

fixtures.headline: India Open Home White-Ball Season Against West Indies
fixtures.body: India begin their series against West Indies with the first of three ODIs in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27, followed by five T20Is running through October 17, as Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer lead India’s build-up toward the 2027 World Cup.

fixtures.headline: Arsenal Visit Brighton as Sunderland Host Man City
fixtures.body: League leaders Arsenal travel to Brighton on September 19-20, while Sunderland — fresh off their first European win in 53 years — host Manchester City in a Premier League weekend that could reshape the top of the table.

fixtures.headline: Baku’s Long Brake Zone Looms as Ferrari Probe Continues
fixtures.body: F1 heads to Baku for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Saturday, September 26, where the circuit’s long run to Turn 1 will be the first real test of whatever fix Ferrari applies after Hamilton’s brake failure in Madrid, per Grandprix.com (Sep 14).

portfolio.headline: Oracle’s Record AI Cloud Backlog Keeps Fueling Investor Optimism
portfolio.body: Oracle shares are still riding the fiscal Q1 report (Sep 10), which showed adjusted EPS of $1.92 on 30% revenue growth to a record $19.35 billion, with cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubling to $7.4 billion. The company booked over $30 billion in new AI contracts without added infrastructure spending, pushing its remaining performance-obligations backlog to $664 billion and prompting guidance for 30–34% cloud revenue growth next quarter, per Yahoo Finance.

portfolio.headline: Boeing CEO Flags 737 MAX Production Shortfall and Cash-Flow Strain
portfolio.body: Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told the Morgan Stanley Laguna Conference (Sep 16) that stabilizing 737 MAX output at the targeted 47 aircraft a month is taking longer than expected, citing manufacturing constraints in key components like wings. He also said hitting the midpoint of the company’s $1–3 billion free cash flow guidance is increasingly challenging, pointing to possible charges on fixed-price defense programs, delayed 787 engine deliveries and a slower-than-hoped 777X certification timeline — concerns that outweighed a Korean Air fleet commitment disclosed the same day.

portfolio.headline: Intel Draws Analyst Price-Target Hikes on AI Turnaround, 18A Ramp
portfolio.body: Tigress Financial raised its Intel price target to $145 from $118 with a Buy rating, citing an AI-driven turnaround and stronger Xeon demand, while Northland upgraded the stock to Outperform with a $120 target, per StocksToTrade (Sep 16). The move followed news that Intel’s High-NA EUV lithography has entered high-volume manufacturing, with more than a million wafers processed across the 18A and Panther Lake platforms, plus plans for roughly a 10% price increase on PC processors starting in October.

portfolio.headline: Rackspace Rides Nvidia Blackwell Partnership Momentum
portfolio.body: Rackspace Technology shares remain buoyed by its Sep 10 announcement that it joined Nvidia’s Cloud Partner Program, launching Blackwell-powered AI infrastructure for regulated enterprises and governments built alongside Palantir software. That sovereign-AI push follows an August Chief AI Officer hire and a Q2 report showing $670 million in quarterly revenue, per Rackspace’s investor relations site.

portfolio.headline: Coeur Mining Cools as Precious-Metals Sentiment Softens
portfolio.body: Coeur Mining is pulling back from its late-August highs as bearish sentiment on near-term gold and silver price direction weighs on miners broadly, per StocksToTrade (Sep 16). The retreat comes despite strong underlying fundamentals — roughly 42% gross margin, an EBITDA margin above 50% and low debt — that traders say provide fundamental support even as the metals cool from recent peaks.

portfolio.headline: Figma Picks Up Cautious ‘Sector Weight’ Coverage From KeyBanc
portfolio.body: Figma drew fresh analyst attention after KeyBanc Capital Markets initiated coverage on Sep 14 with a Sector Weight rating, adding to an ongoing debate among analysts over the design-software company’s growth trajectory against larger rivals like Adobe and Salesforce. No additional company-specific announcement was found for the session.

portfolio.headline: Beyond Meat Stays Volatile as a Heavily Shorted Retail Favorite
portfolio.body: No fresh company-specific catalyst was found for Beyond Meat’s session; the stock remains a heavily shorted, retail-trader-favored name prone to sharp swings. The most recent operational news is the launch of its Beyond Steak Filet at Erewhon and a new “Phytosphere” platform of protein powders and bars, part of an effort to diversify beyond its core burger and sausage lines after Q2 revenue of $68.83 million, an 8.2% year-over-year decline.

stories.headline: Modi Marks 76th Birthday as Murmu, Leaders Hail 25 Years of Governance
stories.body: President Droupadi Murmu led birthday tributes to PM Modi, crediting him with “establish[ing] many new benchmarks of good governance” over 25 years as chief minister and prime minister. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan said India “is shining as a bright spot in the world and among the fastest-growing major economies,” while sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik marked the day with a 25-foot installation on Puri Beach lit by 2,500 earthen lamps, per WION (Sep 17).

stories.headline: Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026, Touts India’s Chip Talent Pool
stories.body: PM Modi opened the three-day SEMICON India 2026 at Delhi’s Yashobhoomi, where over 600 exhibitors — roughly 300 of them international — are showcasing India’s semiconductor ecosystem under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem.” Modi told industry leaders that “India’s talent pool, combined with the experience and capabilities of global industry leaders, can create significant opportunities,” per Free Press Journal (Sep 17).

stories.headline: US House Passes Bill Empowering Trump to Slap 100% Tariffs on India, China
stories.body: The US House passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 262-159 on Sep 16, following the Senate’s 86-11 approval in August, giving President Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy — squarely targeting India and China. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the move, saying “during the war, it is sometimes better to make a not-so-perfect decision than to do nothing,” per WION (Sep 17).

stories.headline: Surging Gilt Yields Squeeze Chancellor Healey’s Budget Headroom
stories.body: Rising UK borrowing costs have eaten into roughly £10 billion of the £23.6 billion fiscal headroom the OBR forecast in March, with national debt near £3 trillion and annual interest payments topping £100 billion, per The Spectator Australia (Sep 14). Commentator John O’Neill warned the UK is “often the worst-hit nation thanks to our ‘moron premium’” as traders bet on further rate rises ahead of the OBR’s updated forecast due Oct 28.

stories.headline: UK Inflation Jumps to 3.1% as Bank of England Meets on Rates
stories.body: Consumer prices rose 3.1% year-on-year in August, up from 2.9% in July and 2.6% in June, with the ONS’s Grant Fitzner pointing to “rising crude oil and petrol prices” and higher airfares, per MoneyWeek (Sep 15). The Bank of England’s rate-setters meet today, Sep 17, with markets largely expecting the Bank Rate to be held at 3.75% despite the inflation uptick.

stories.headline: RMT Suspends Strike Action on East Midlands Railway for Sep 16-17
stories.body: The RMT union called off planned strikes at East Midlands Railway covering Wednesday and Thursday, letting the operator run a full timetable even as “Action Short of Strike” continues over safety concerns with the Class 810 train fleet, per Rail Business Daily (Sep 14). RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey said it was “disappointing that EMR will not accept simple union demands around unsolicited brake applications and the Aux On/Off failures,” while EMR’s Philippa Cresswell welcomed the pause as a chance “to continue our discussions” toward resolution.

stories.headline: Investigation Ties Covert Israeli Cell to Anti-Qatar Influence Campaign
stories.body: A joint investigation found that around 30 people, including Israeli psychological-warfare experts and a former Mossad official, ran a covert influence campaign against Qatar via a WhatsApp group called “Free the Kidnapped,” launched days after October 7, 2023 and halted about a month later, per Al Jazeera (Sep 15). “It is unlikely such a campaign would exist without the motivation of an actor like Israel,” said Marc Owen Jones of Northwestern University, while King’s College London’s Andreas Krieg noted “Israel has spent years presenting Qatar as an enabler of Hamas, yet at the same time successive Israeli governments have relied on Qatar.”

stories.headline: Qatar Central Bank Raises Key Interest Rates by 25 Basis Points
stories.body: The Qatar Central Bank lifted its deposit, lending and repo rates by 25 basis points each, to 4.10%, 4.60% and 4.35% respectively, effective Thursday, Sep 17, following its latest monetary policy review, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 16). The move tracks the wider Gulf tightening cycle as dollar-pegged regional currencies keep pace with US rate policy.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia Vows ‘Firm’ Response After Houthi Strikes Wound 13
stories.body: Houthi missile and drone attacks on Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif wounded 13 civilians and damaged homes and vehicles, prompting coalition spokesperson Major-General Turki al-Maliki to warn that “the Joint Forces Command of the Coalition will deal with these attacks responsibly and firmly to protect the sovereignty of the kingdom,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 15). The Houthis claimed Saudi Arabia carried out 54 air raids in 24 hours, as the UN reported 125,000 people newly displaced in Yemen since early September.

doha_events.headline: Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion Opens at MIA
doha_events.body: The Museum of Islamic Art has opened “Uzbekistan: Heritage in Motion,” running September 3 through November 28 in the Sheikh Saoud Al Thani Temporary Exhibitions Gallery, per Qatar Living (Aug 26). The show brings together 146 objects spanning the 8th century to today, including a 7th-century wall painting from Samarkand’s Ambassadors’ Hall and a 15th-century astrolabe, curated in partnership with Uzbekistan’s Art and Culture Development Foundation.

doha_events.headline: Taha Desouky Brings Stand-Up to Al Mayassa Theater
doha_events.body: Comedian Taha Desouky performs at the Al Mayassa Theater, QNCC, tonight, Thursday September 17, with doors opening at 9pm, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 16). Tickets start from QR 285.

doha_events.headline: Qatar Philharmonic Performs “Sounds of Mexico”
doha_events.body: The Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra performs “Sounds of Mexico” at QNCC on September 18, conducted by Enrique Arturo Diemecke as part of the Qatar–Mexico 2026 Year of Culture concert series, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 6). Tickets are on sale now through Platinumlist; a companion “Sounds of Canada” concert, led by Charles Olivieri-Munroe, follows on November 7.

doha_events.headline: Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition Returns to DECC
doha_events.body: The Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition runs September 28 through October 3 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre in West Bay, featuring more than 500 brands and typically drawing around 30,000 visitors, per Qatar Living (Sep 6). Admission is free, but visitors must complete registration through Visit Qatar in advance rather than assume walk-in access.
